definition_en: trust that allows later payment, praise for something done, or a unit of study
core_image: 店主在小本子上写下你的名字，让你下个月再付钱
scene: 小店的老板没要现金，只在本子上写下他的名字。 The shop gave him credit and let him pay next month.
sceneCN: 这里 credit 指「赊账」（第 1 个义项：先拿货后付款的信任）；句意是店家让他赊账，下个月再付钱。

senses.title: Buy now, pay later
senses.definition: an arrangement to take goods now and pay for them later
senses.definitionCN: 先取货、后付款的安排
senses.example: He bought the bicycle on credit.
senses.exampleCN: 他赊账买了那辆自行车。
senses.why: Trust is written in a book and becomes money.
senses.whyCN: 信任被写进本子，就变成了钱。

senses.title: Praise for what was done
senses.definition: praise or approval given to someone for an act
senses.definitionCN: 因某件事给予某人的称赞或认可
senses.example: She deserves credit for the rescue.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援她功不可没。
senses.why: A good act is entered under the name of the doer.
senses.whyCN: 一件好事会被记在做这件事的人名下。

senses.title: A unit of study
senses.definition: a unit that measures work completed in a course
senses.definitionCN: 衡量一门课程完成量的单位
senses.example: The course carries four credits.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课有四个学分。
senses.why: Hours in class are counted and stored like money.
senses.whyCN: 上课的时数被数出来，像钱一样存着。

intro.en: Credit goes back to Latin credere, to believe, and creditum, a thing entrusted.
intro.cn: credit 可追到拉丁语 credere（相信）与 creditum（托付之物）。

items.en: Credere meant to believe a person or a report.
items.cn: credere 意为相信一个人或一则说法。

items.en: Creditum named money or goods entrusted to another.
items.cn: creditum 指托付给他人的钱或货物。

items.en: Credit named trust placed in a person.
items.cn: credit 指对一个人寄予的信任。

items.en: Credit came to mean trust that allows later payment.
items.cn: credit 开始指允许延后付款的信任。

items.en: Banks turned that trust into formal accounts.
items.cn: 银行把这种信任变成了正式账户。

items.en: It also means praise and a unit of study.
items.cn: 它也表示赞扬与一种学业单位。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- stem of believing, and the meaning group names trust and borrowed money.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示相信的 cred- 词干，近义组列出信任与借款的说法。

entries.definition: a short statement of belief
able to be believed
a proof of a person's right or skill
entries.definitionCN: 证明资格或本领的凭据

entries.definition: firm belief in someone
money lent and to be repaid
words that approve of someone

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a name in a shop book to a line of praise in a report.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从店本子上的一个名字，跑到报告里的一句赞扬。

normal.en: Credit and creed share a root: both rest on belief.
normal.cn: credit 与 creed 同根：两者都立在相信上。

normal.en: The shop trusts the name, not the face.
normal.cn: 店信的是那个名字，不是那张脸。

normal.en: Praise is credit paid into a person's account.
normal.cn: 赞扬是存进某人账户的一笔信用。

normal.en: A credit is a coin called an hour of class.
normal.cn: 学分是一枚叫一课时的硬币。

normal.en: Write it down, and trust becomes a number.
normal.cn: 写下来，信任就变成一个数字。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook where names stand in for coins.
abstract.cn: 想象一个本子，名字代替了硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand and a nod of approval.
abstract.cn: 想象一只举起的手和一个赞许的点头。

abstract.en: Picture a card that buys without cash.
abstract.cn: 想象一张不用现金就能买东西的卡。

examples.en: They let her buy the coat on credit.
examples.cn: 他们让她赊账买了那件外套。

examples.en: He got credit for the whole idea.
examples.cn: 整个主意都算作他的功劳。

examples.en: This class is worth two credits.
examples.cn: 这门课值两个学分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 credit 记成 cred（相信）加 -it：先相信你，才让你先拿货后付钱，也才把功劳记在你名下。

root: 源自拉丁语 credere（相信）与 creditum（托付之物）；本义是相信并托付，由这份信任生出赊账、信誉、功劳与学分诸义。

sensesIntro.en: From trust that lets you pay later, to the praise and the study points that trust earns.
sensesIntro.cn: 从允许你延后付款的信任，到这份信任换来的赞扬与学分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shopkeeper writing a name in a small book.
core.cn: 核心意象：店主在一个小本子上写下名字。

branches.en: Trust in a buyer turns into a written account.
branches.cn: 对买主的信任变成了一笔账面记录。

branches.en: Praise is a kind of credit paid to a person.
branches.cn: 赞扬是付给某个人的一种信用。

branches.en: Class hours are counted as credits in a school.
branches.cn: 在学校里，课时被计成学分。

branches.en: The shop book and the school record both count what is owed or done.
branches.cn: 店本与学籍记录都在数着欠下的和做完的。

branches.en: A name in a report can shine as brightly as money.
branches.cn: 报告里的一个名字可以和钱一样发亮。

intro.en: Credit sits in the Latin cred- family of believing, together with creed and credible.
intro.cn: credit 属于拉丁语 cred-（相信）这一族，creed 与 credible 也在其中。

latinIntro.en: The Latin credere, to believe, is the root behind every word here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 credere（相信）是这里每个词背后的根。

items.exampleCN: 信用让这笔交易成为可能。

items.meaning: one to whom money is owed

items.example: Show your credentials at the desk.
items.exampleCN: 在服务台出示你的证件。
银行喜欢信用良好的买家。
这条消息使那说法不可信。

definition_en: to deal with a difficult situation or a heavy load
core_image: 一个人低着头顶着风走，衣角被吹得笔直
scene: 停水三天，邻居们轮流去远处打水。 Some families coped by sharing water with their neighbours.
sceneCN: 这里 cope 指「应对」（第 1 个义项：面对困难局面并设法撑住）；句意是有些家庭靠与邻居分水来应对。

senses.title: To get through a hard time
senses.definition: to manage a difficult situation with the means you have
senses.definitionCN: 用手上有的办法撑过一个困难局面
senses.example: They coped with the loss of power for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 他们撑过了一个星期没电的日子。
senses.why: A storm does not ask whether you are ready; it asks whether you can stand.
senses.whyCN: 风暴不问你准备好没有，只问你能不能站住。

senses.title: To handle a task well enough
senses.definition: to deal with a problem or duty without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或职责处理得过去，而不至于崩掉
senses.example: She copes with three jobs and a family.
senses.exampleCN: 她要应付三份工作和一个家庭。
senses.why: Not every day is won; some are simply carried to the end.
senses.whyCN: 不是每一天都算赢，有些日子只是被撑到了尽头。

intro.en: Cope comes from Old French couper, to strike or cut, from Latin colaphus, a blow, from Greek kolaphos.
intro.cn: cope 来自古法语 couper（打、切），源于拉丁语 colaphus（一击），更早出自希腊语 kolaphos。

items.en: Kolaphos meant a blow with the fist.
items.cn: kolaphos 意为用拳头打的一击。

items.en: Colaphus kept the sense of a blow or a buffet.
items.cn: colaphus 保留了打击或掌击的含义。

items.en: Old French couper meant to strike or cut.
items.cn: 古法语 couper 意为击打或切割。

items.en: English cope first meant to fight or come to blows with someone.
items.cn: 英语 cope 最初意为与某人交手或打起来。

items.en: The sense shifted from fighting to handling a burden.
items.cn: 词义从打斗转向承担与应付。

items.en: Today it almost always appears with with.
items.cn: 今天它几乎总是与 with 一同出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short -ope shape, and the meaning group names other verbs for facing difficulty.
note.cn: 形近组共享短短的 -ope 外形，近义组列出其他面对困难的说法。

entries.definition: a thing made to match another
a police officer in informal speech
the range a subject or plan covers
entries.definitionCN: 某主题或计划覆盖的范围

entries.definition: to succeed in dealing with something
to deal with a situation or person
entries.definitionCN: 处理某种局面或某个人

entries.definition: to bear something painful for a long time

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a person walking into wind, then move to too many duties held at once.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个人逆风行走开始，再到同时压来的过多职责。

normal.en: Cope almost always travels with with, because no one copes alone with nothing.
normal.cn: cope 几乎总和 with 同行，因为没人能空着手独自应付。

normal.en: The old sense was to trade blows; now you trade blows with a problem.
normal.cn: 它古时指交手；现在你是和一个问题交手。

normal.en: Think of a small boat riding a big wave: it does not stop the wave.
normal.cn: 想象小船压过大浪：它没有让浪停下。

normal.en: Coping is not winning; it is staying afloat.
normal.cn: 应对不是取胜，而是还浮在水面。

normal.en: One letter away from copy, but nothing here is copied.
normal.cn: 它和 copy 只差一个字母，但这里没有什么是抄来的。

abstract.en: Picture a walker leaning into a strong wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一个行人倾身顶着大风。

abstract.en: Picture a table piled with boxes and one steady hand beneath.
abstract.cn: 想象堆满箱子的桌子下，有一只手稳稳托着。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge holding while the river pushes.
abstract.cn: 想象河水冲压时，一座桥仍然撑住。

examples.en: He copes with pressure by running every morning.
examples.cn: 他每天早晨跑步来应对压力。

examples.en: The staff coped well when the system failed.
examples.cn: 系统出故障时，员工应付得很好。

examples.en: Some students find it hard to cope with the pace.
examples.cn: 有些学生觉得难以应付这种节奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cope 记成一个人顶着风走：风不会停，能走过去就是应付。

root: 源自希腊语 kolaphos（一拳），经拉丁语 colaphus 与古法语 couper（击打）进入英语，本指交手，后转为承担与应付。

sensesIntro.en: From trading blows with an opponent, to standing under a load that will not lift.
sensesIntro.cn: 从与对手交手，到站在一份不会变轻的重担之下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leaning into a hard wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人倾身顶着强风。

branches.en: A hard time is met with whatever means are at hand.
branches.cn: 困难时期，用手边有的办法去迎。

branches.en: A duty is carried through without collapse.
branches.cn: 一份职责被撑到最后，人没有垮。

branches.en: Both senses are about standing while pressure stays.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关乎压力仍在时站稳。

branches.en: The first is short and sharp, like a storm.
branches.cn: 第一个义项短而急，像一场风暴。

branches.en: The second is long and quiet, like a daily load.
branches.cn: 第二个义项长而静，像每天的负担。

intro.en: Cope reached English through Old French couper, to strike, from Latin colaphus, a blow.
intro.cn: cope 经古法语 couper（击打）进入英语，源于拉丁语 colaphus（一击）。

latinIntro.en: Cope keeps company with short look-alikes such as copy and cop rather than with a Latin base.
latinIntro.cn: cope 更多与 copy、cop 这类短小形近词为伴，而没有留下常用的拉丁词基。

items.meaning: the act or way of dealing with stress
items.meaningCN: 应对压力的行为或方式

items.meaning: an easy way of avoiding a duty

items.example: A copyist made the fair copy.
items.exampleCN: 一名抄写员誊出了定稿。

definition_en: finely chopped meat packed into a thin casing
core_image: 平底锅里几根香肠滋滋作响，表皮变成金棕色
scene: 早餐时，平底锅里煎着几根香肠。 Two sausages are frying in the pan.
sceneCN: 这里 sausage 是「香肠」（第 1 个义项）；句意：两根香肠正在锅里煎着。

senses.title: Meat in a casing
senses.definition: finely chopped meat packed into a thin casing
senses.definitionCN: 切碎后灌入细肠衣的肉
senses.example: They grilled sausages for lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 他们午餐烤了香肠。
senses.why: The core sense is chopped meat shaped by a casing.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是用肠衣定型的碎肉。

senses.title: Processed sausage product
senses.definition: a manufactured meat product sold in a sausage shape
senses.definitionCN: 做成香肠形状出售的加工肉制品
senses.example: He bought a packet of sausage snacks.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一包香肠零食。
senses.why: The casing shape extends to industrial meat products.
senses.whyCN: 肠衣的形状扩展到工业肉制品。

senses.title: Sausage shape
senses.definition: something long and rounded like a sausage
senses.definitionCN: 像香肠一样细长而圆的东西
senses.example: The balloon was twisted into a sausage shape.
senses.exampleCN: 气球被扭成了香肠的形状。
senses.why: The food shape becomes a way to describe other objects.
senses.whyCN: 食物形状成为描述其他物体的方式。

intro.en: Sausage traces from Latin salsus through Late Latin salsicia and Old French.
intro.cn: sausage 经晚期拉丁语 salsicia 和古法语，追溯到拉丁语 salsus。

items.en: Salsus means salted.
items.cn: salsus 意为盐腌的。

items.en: Salsicia named salted meat preparations.
items.cn: salsicia 指盐腌的肉类食品。

items.en: Saussiche named a seasoned meat casing.
items.cn: saussiche 指调味肉肠。

items.en: Sausige appeared for minced meat in a skin.
items.cn: sausige 指灌在肠衣中的碎肉。

items.en: Sausage covers fresh, cured, and industrial products.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sausage 兼指鲜肠、腊肠和工业制品。

note.en: Sausage is compared with look-alike words and other meat products.
note.cn: 把 sausage 与形近词和其他肉制品作比较。

entries.definition: a flavoured liquid for food
a small dish under a cup
an aromatic herb
a sausage served in a long bun
a cured sausage sliced thin
a spicy cured sausage

normalIntro.en: Sausage can be remembered by its salt root and its shape.
normalIntro.cn: 可以从盐腌词根和细长形状两方面记住 sausage。

normal.en: Sausage begins like sauce, because both come from salted food.
normal.cn: sausage 开头像 sauce，因为两者都源自盐腌食物。

normal.en: The long body of the word looks like a sausage link.
normal.cn: 这个单词长长的词形像一截香肠。

normal.en: Sausages are often fried, so picture them in a hot pan.
normal.cn: 香肠常被煎，想象它们在热锅里。

normal.en: A sausage roll wraps the meat in pastry.
normal.cn: 香肠卷把肉包在酥皮里。

normal.en: The plural sausages adds s and keeps the soft ge sound.
normal.cn: 复数 sausages 加 s，并保留柔和的 ge 音。

abstract.en: A casing turns scattered meat into one neat form.
abstract.cn: 肠衣把零散的肉变成一个整齐的整体。

abstract.en: Salt once preserved meat through long winters.
abstract.cn: 盐曾经帮助人们在漫长冬季保存肉类。

abstract.en: The sausage shape is simple enough to describe almost anything.
abstract.cn: 香肠的形状简单到几乎可以形容任何东西。

examples.en: She sliced the sausage for the pasta.
examples.cn: 她把香肠切片放进意面。

examples.en: The smell of fried sausage filled the kitchen.
examples.cn: 煎香肠的香味充满了厨房。

examples.en: He ate a sausage roll on the train.
examples.cn: 他在火车上吃了一个香肠卷。

dict_mnemonic.text: sausage 与 sauce 同源，都和盐腌有关，可记「用盐腌好、灌进肠衣的肉」。

root: 源自拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的），经晚期拉丁语 salsicia 与古法语 saussiche 进入英语，核心义「盐腌碎肉灌成的肠」。

sensesIntro.en: Sausage means chopped meat in a casing, a processed meat product, or a sausage shape.
sensesIntro.cn: sausage 意为灌在肠衣里的碎肉、加工肉制品，或香肠形状。

core.en: Salted chopped meat shaped inside a casing.
core.cn: 在肠衣中定型的盐腌碎肉。

branches.en: The core food, meat packed in a casing.
branches.cn: 核心食物，灌入肠衣的肉。

branches.en: Manufactured meat products in sausage form.
branches.cn: 做成香肠形状的加工肉制品。

branches.en: Any object with a long rounded shape.
branches.cn: 任何细长浑圆的物体。

branches.en: Both are meat sold in a casing or tube.
branches.cn: 两者都是肠衣或管状包装出售的肉。

branches.en: The industrial product keeps the food shape.
branches.cn: 工业制品保留了食物的形状。

intro.en: Sausage belongs to the salted-food family of sauce.
intro.cn: sausage 属于 sauce 的盐腌食物词族。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin salsus, salted.
latinIntro.cn: 其词根是拉丁语 salsus（盐腌的）。

items.example: Mix the sausage meat with herbs.
items.exampleCN: 把香肠肉馅和香草拌在一起。

items.example: His saucy joke made us laugh.
items.exampleCN: 他俏皮的笑话逗笑了我们。
萨尔萨辣酱配薯片很好。

latinEntries.example: Sal is the Latin word for salt.

definition_zh: 争论；争吵；论点；论据；论证；内容的梗概
definition_en: a disagreement or quarrel, a set of reasons offered for a claim, or the main idea of a book or talk
core_image: 桌面上摊开的一串理由，一条接一条扣住结论
scene: 会议室里，白板写满箭头和方框。 Her argument was built on three pieces of evidence.
sceneCN: 这里 argument 是「论点；论证」（第 2 个义项：为支持某个主张而给出的一组理由）；句意为「她的论证建立在三份证据之上」。画面里有会议室白板、箭头与方框。

pos.zh: 名词：争论；争吵；论点；论据；论证；内容梗概

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ment 得到的动词，义为「争论；论证」
由本词加 -ative 构成，义为「好争辩的」
由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「论证；论辩」
由 argue 加 -able 构成，义为「可论证的；有争议的」

senses.title: A spoken disagreement
senses.definition: a disagreement, usually spoken, in which people are angry with each other
senses.definitionCN: 通常以言语进行、双方带着怒气的意见冲突
senses.example: They had an argument about money last night.
senses.exampleCN: 昨晚他们为钱吵了一架。
senses.why: The noun names the noisy end of arguere: two people each trying to make their point clear at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名 arguere 那个吵嚷的端点：两个人同时各讲各的道理。

senses.title: A set of reasons
senses.definition: a set of reasons given to support or oppose a claim
senses.definitionCN: 为支持或反对某个主张而给出的一组理由
senses.example: Her argument was built on three pieces of evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论证建立在三份证据之上。
senses.why: Here the proofs are laid out one after another until the claim is clear.
senses.whyCN: 这里的证据一条接一条摆开，直到主张变得清楚。

senses.title: The process of reasoning
senses.definition: the process of reasoning from evidence to a conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 从证据推进到结论的推理过程
senses.example: The argument takes five steps from data to conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证从数据到结论共分五步。
senses.why: The noun also names the movement of thought, not only its result.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也命名思路的移动，而不只是移动的结果。

senses.title: The main idea of a work
senses.definition: the main idea or summary of a book, play, or talk
senses.definitionCN: 一本书、一部戏剧或一场讲话的主要意思或提要
senses.example: The argument of the essay appears in the first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的梗概出现在第一段。
senses.why: A book's spine is its clearest line of reasoning, summarized for readers.
senses.whyCN: 一本书的骨干，就是它最清晰的推理线索，被概括给读者。

intro.en: Argument is the noun of argue, and its two branches are noise and proof.
intro.cn: argument 是 argue 的名词，它的两条分支分别是吵嚷与证据。

items.en: Arguere meant 'to make clear, prove, accuse'; its own origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: arguere 意为「使清楚、证明、指控」；它自身的来源存疑。

items.en: Argumentum is 'a proof, a argument, a subject', the noun built on the verb.
items.cn: argumentum 是建立在那个动词上的名词，意为「证据、论证、题材」。

items.en: Old French passes the noun into English, where both the dispute and the proof sense take root.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带进英语，争吵与论证两义都在此扎根。

items.en: The word is recorded in the fourteenth century with the sense of reasoning.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪有记录，带有推理的意思。

items.en: The noun now names quarrels, cases, reasoning and the gist of a work.
items.cn: 这个名词现在命名争吵、主张、推理，以及作品的要点。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the argue family; the near-meaning group gathers words for disputes and reasoning.
note.cn: 形近组收 argue 的词族；近义组收表示争执与推理的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to quarrel or give reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 本词由它加 -ment 构成，义为「争吵、论证」的动词。

entries.definition: Inclined to argue.
The systematic presentation of arguments.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「论证、论辩」，指系统地提出理由。

entries.definition: Open to debate or able to be supported.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可论证的、有争议的」。

entries.definition: A serious disagreement, often public or legal.
entries.definitionCN: 严重的分歧，常公开或涉及法律，比 argument 更正式。

entries.definition: The process of thinking logically toward a conclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 朝结论进行的逻辑思考过程，对应 argument 的论证义。

entries.definition: The arguments and evidence for one side.
entries.definitionCN: 一方所持的理由与证据，与 argument 的论据义接近。

entries.definition: A formal discussion of opposing arguments.
entries.definitionCN: 正反论点之间的正式讨论。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the two branches of the noun: the shout and the proof.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子抓住这个名词的两条分支：喊叫与证据。

normal.en: Argue plus -ment: the thing produced by arguing.
normal.cn: argue 加 -ment：争辩所产生的东西。

normal.en: A quarrel is the loud branch of the noun.
normal.cn: 争吵是这个名词吵闹的那条分支。

normal.en: A case built of evidence is the proof branch.
normal.cn: 用证据搭起来的案子，是论证那条分支。

normal.en: The steps from data to conclusion are the argument itself.
normal.cn: 从数据走到结论的那些步骤，就是论证本身。

normal.en: The gist of a book is its argument in brief.
normal.cn: 一本书的要点，就是它被压缩后的论证。

abstract.en: One noun covers a fight and a proof.
abstract.cn: 一个名词同时覆盖一场架与一份证明。

abstract.en: Both are attempts to make something clear.
abstract.cn: 两者都是想把某事讲清的尝试。

abstract.en: The word asks whether a claim can stand on its reasons.
abstract.cn: 这个词在问：一个主张能否靠它的理由站住。

examples.en: They had an argument about money last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚他们为钱吵了一架。

examples.en: Her argument was built on three pieces of evidence.
examples.cn: 她的论证建立在三份证据之上。

examples.en: The argument of the essay appears in the first paragraph.
examples.cn: 这篇文章的梗概出现在第一段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿格尤门特」——桌上摊开一串理由，一条扣一条，最后扣住结论：论点；争论

root: argument 是 argue 的名词，来自拉丁语 argumentum「证据、论证、题材」，其动词 arguere 意为「使清楚、证明、指控」，更早的来源存疑。这个词因此天然带着两条分支：两个人抢着把道理讲清，就成了一场争吵；把证据一条条摆开、推到结论，就成了一套论据与论证过程；而一本书或一场讲话的推理主线被压缩起来，就是它的内容梗概。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all present reasons or their absence: a quarrel, a case, the steps of reasoning, and a work's main idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都在呈现理由或理由的缺失：争吵、论据、推理步骤，以及一部作品的主要意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of cards laid on a table, each one pointing to the next, ending at a claim.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一排卡片，每张都指向下一张，最后指向一个主张。

branches.en: THE NOISE LINE: both sides shout their case at once.
branches.cn: 吵嚷线：双方同时喊出自己的理由。

branches.en: THE CASE LINE: reasons are arranged to support a claim.
branches.cn: 论据线：理由被排布起来支持一个主张。

branches.en: THE STEPS LINE: the noun names the path of thought.
branches.cn: 步骤线：这个名词命名思路的行进路径。

branches.en: THE SUMMARY LINE: a work's spine is its argument in brief.
branches.cn: 梗概线：一部作品的骨干就是压缩后的论证。

branches.en: THE REASONING LINE: case and process are one structure.
branches.cn: 推理线：论据与过程是同一个结构。

intro.en: Argument is argue plus -ment, and the Latin noun argumentum sits behind both.
intro.cn: argument 是 argue 加 -ment，两者背后都站着拉丁名词 argumentum。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is real: argumentum is the noun of arguere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：argumentum 就是 arguere 的名词。

items.exampleCN: 这番论证说服了陪审团。

items.example: Her argumentation was clear and calm.

items.exampleCN: 他回应了每一个反方论点。

items.meaning: the final speech in a trial
items.example: The closing argument lasted an hour.
items.exampleCN: 结案陈词持续了一小时。

items.example: The court heard oral argument in May.
items.exampleCN: 法院在五月听取了口头辩论。

items.example: She made a strong argument for reform.
items.exampleCN: 她为改革提出了有力的论证。

definition_zh: 可能性；概率；赔率；不和；不利条件
definition_en: the chance that something will or will not happen, the figures that show this chance in betting, a state of disagreement, and the difficulties that work against success
core_image: 赛马场边的木牌上，一串数字跟着人群的喊声上下翻动
scene: 赛马场的围栏边挤满了人，看台上的示数牌随着下注一笔笔变动，有人低声算着自己那匹马的机会。 The odds on the grey horse fell as the crowd put money down.
sceneCN: 这里的 odds 是「赔率」（第 2 个义项：博彩中表示机会大小的数字）；句意为随着人群下注，那匹灰马的赔率下降了。图中可辨识物件：围栏、示数牌、马匹。

pos.zh: 可能性；概率；赔率；不和；不利条件

derivatives.zh: odds 是 odd 的复数形式；odd 由古诺尔斯语 oddi 进入英语，义为「单数的；奇怪的」
由 odd 加 -ity 构成，义为「怪事；怪人」，与 odds 同出一源
由 odd 与 ball 复合而成，义为「古怪的人」

senses.title: The chance that something will happen
senses.definition: how likely it is that something will happen, often stated as a comparison between the chances of two outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能程度，常以两种结果的 chance 相互比较来表示
senses.example: The odds of finding a seat after noon are very low.
senses.exampleCN: 过了中午还想找到座位的可能性很低。
senses.why: The plural of odd once meant things that do not match, and unequal chances are exactly what probability compares, so odds became the name for the imbalance itself.
senses.whyCN: odd 的复数最初指彼此不相配的东西，而不相等的机会正是概率所要比较的，于是 odds 成了这种「不平衡」本身的名字。

senses.title: The figures offered in betting
senses.definition: the numbers set by a bookmaker to show how much a winning bet pays compared with the stake
senses.definitionCN: 博彩庄家设定的数字，表示中奖时能拿到多少钱与本金相比
senses.example: The odds on the outsider were fifty to one.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹冷门马的赔率是五十比一。
senses.why: Once people bet on unequal chances, the ratio of those chances becomes a price, and the word for imbalance turns into the figures on the board.
senses.whyCN: 人们一旦为不相等的机会下注，这些机会的比值就变成价格，表示「不平衡」的词也就变成了牌子上的数字。

senses.title: A state of disagreement
senses.definition: a condition in which two people, groups or accounts do not agree and are in conflict
senses.definitionCN: 两方人或两套说法互不同意、彼此冲突的状态
senses.example: The two managers have been at odds for months.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位经理已经不和好几个月了。
senses.why: Two things at odds are pulling in different directions, which is the same picture of things that fail to match, moved from numbers to people.
senses.whyCN: 处于 at odds 的两样东西朝不同方向使劲，仍是「对不上」这个画面，只是从数字挪到了人身上。

senses.title: Difficulties working against success
senses.definition: the unfavourable circumstances that make success less likely and must be overcome
senses.definitionCN: 使成功更困难、必须加以克服的不利情况
senses.example: She finished the race against all the odds.
senses.exampleCN: 她克服重重不利条件跑完了比赛。
senses.why: If odds measure how much the chances favour one side, then whatever stands on the weaker side is the odds against you, and the word comes to name hardship itself.
senses.whyCN: 如果 odds 衡量机会偏向哪一方，那么站在较弱一方的就是「对你不利的 odds」，这个词于是用来指艰难本身。

intro.en: Odds is the plural of odd, and odd came into English from Old Norse; the betting and disagreement senses grew out of the old idea of things that do not match.
intro.cn: odds 是 odd 的复数，而 odd 经古诺尔斯语进入英语；赔率与不和这两个义项，都是从「彼此不相配」这个旧意思里长出来的。

items.en: Oddi named a point, a triangle or an unpaired third item, and Norse settlers brought the word into English speech.
items.cn: oddi 指尖角、三角形或落单的第三个东西，诺尔斯移民把这个词带进了英语口语。

items.en: English used odd first for numbers that cannot be divided into two equal parts, then for anything left over or unlike the rest.
items.cn: 英语最初用 odd 指不能平分为两份的数，随后指任何剩下的或与其余不同的东西。

items.en: The plural odds named unequal things or a difference between sides, a sense recorded long before betting took it up.
items.cn: 复数形式 odds 指不相等的事物或两方的差额，这一义项在博彩采用它之前很久就有记录。

items.en: Bookmakers began to quote odds as the ratio between the money staked and the money paid, and the word settled into that everyday use.
items.cn: 庄家开始用 odds 报出下注金额与赔付金额之间的比值，这个词便在博彩的日常用法中固定下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the plural form for chance, betting figures, disagreement in the phrase at odds, and the hardships summed up in against the odds.
items.cn: 现代英语保留复数形式，用来指机会、投注数字、at odds 一语中的不和，以及 against the odds 所概括的艰难。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family around odd; the near-meaning group collects words for chance, betting and open disagreement.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕 odd 的词族；近义组收表示机会、博彩以及公开分歧的词。

entries.definition: An unpaired number, or something strange and unexpected.
entries.definitionCN: 不成对的数，或奇怪、出人意料的事物。

entries.definition: A strange thing or a person who seems unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 古怪的事物，或显得不寻常的人。

entries.definition: A person whose behaviour strikes others as strange.
entries.definitionCN: 行为让人觉得古怪的人。

entries.definition: In a way that is strange or unexpected.
entries.definitionCN: 以奇怪或出人意料的方式。

entries.definition: The chance that something will happen.
A measured chance, often expressed as a figure between zero and one.
entries.definitionCN: 经过度量的可能性，常以零到一之间的数字表示。

entries.definition: The possibility that something may happen, especially when it is not certain.
entries.definitionCN: 某事可能发生的机会，尤指结果不确定时。

entries.definition: A situation in which people hold different views and do not agree.
entries.definitionCN: 人们各持不同看法、彼此不同意的情形。

normalIntro.en: Odds is odd made plural, and the plural carries the old idea of two sides that do not match, which is why chance, prices and quarrels all wear the same word.
normalIntro.cn: odds 是变成复数的 odd，而复数带着「两边对不上」的旧意思，所以机会、价码与口角都穿同一个词。

normal.en: Odd plus -s gives odds, and the plural is permanent: English keeps the s even when the meaning is a single chance.
normal.cn: odd 加 -s 得到 odds，这个复数是固定的：即使意思只是一次机会，英语也保留那个 s。

normal.en: Odd first named what cannot be paired, and odds names two sides whose chances are not level.
normal.cn: odd 最初指无法配对的东西，而 odds 指两边机会并不持平。

normal.en: At odds with someone keeps the picture of two sides pulling apart rather than matching.
normal.cn: at odds with 某人，保留了「两边分开使劲、并不吻合」的画面。

normal.en: Against the odds puts a person on the weaker side of those unequal chances, so the phrase means hardship.
normal.cn: against the odds 把人放到不相等机会中较弱的一边，因此这个说法意味着艰难。

normal.en: The phrase odds and ends survives as 'small leftovers', because odds once meant the extra, unmatched pieces.
normal.cn: odds and ends 作为「零碎杂物」保留下来，因为 odds 曾指多出来、配不上对的那几件。

abstract.en: Odds is the arithmetic of hope: it turns a feeling about the future into something that can be quoted and wagered.
abstract.cn: odds 是希望算术化：它把对未来的感觉变成可以报价、可以下注的东西。

abstract.en: That odds can mean both a probability and a quarrel suggests that disagreement is simply two chances pulling apart.
abstract.cn: odds 既能指概率又能指争吵，说明分歧不过是两个机会在朝两边分开。

abstract.en: To act against the odds is to bet on oneself when the numbers say otherwise.
abstract.cn: 顶着 odds 行事，就是在数字说「不」的时候把赌注押在自己身上。

examples.en: The odds of a late frost this month are quite low.
examples.cn: 这个月出现晚霜的可能性相当低。

examples.en: The bookmaker raised the odds just before the final.
examples.cn: 庄家在决赛前刚刚提高了赔率。

examples.en: He and his old partner have been at odds since the sale.
examples.cn: 自从那次出售之后，他和老搭档就一直不和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「熬的」——机会是熬出来的，赔率也跟着数字走；记住 odds 是可能性与赔率。

root: odd（古诺尔斯语 oddi：尖角、落单的第三个）的复数形式；由「不相配、不相等」引申为可能性、赔率、不和与不利条件。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two sides that do not match; from that imbalance come the measured chance, the price quoted in betting, quarrels between people and the hardship of the weaker side.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两边对不上；由这种不平衡分出被量化的机会、博彩报出的价码、人之间的口角，以及较弱一方所承受的艰难。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scoreboard beside the racecourse where figures flip with every bet placed.
core.cn: 核心意象：赛马场边的示数牌，数字随每一笔下注上下翻动。

branches.en: a person weighing the chance of a seat after noon
branches.cn: 一个人估量下午还能不能找到座位

branches.en: figures on a board rising and falling with the money
branches.cn: 牌子上的数字随钱上下变动

branches.en: two managers refusing to sit at the same table
branches.cn: 两位经理拒绝同席

branches.en: a runner finishing after everyone had given up
branches.cn: 众人都放弃后仍跑完全程的人

branches.en: the same unequal balance seen in sums and in struggle
branches.cn: 数字与挣扎中同一种不平等的衡量

intro.en: The word is a plural noun with a visible adjective behind it, so its parts are odd, the plural ending and the phrases that carry the old idea of uneven sides.
intro.cn: 这个词是复数名词，背后有一个看得见的形容词，所以它的构件是 odd、复数词尾，以及承载「两边不齐」旧意思的若干说法。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for odd or odds, both of which reached English from Old Norse and stand outside the Latin family.
latinIntro.cn: odd 与 odds 都没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，二者都从古诺尔斯语进入英语，属于拉丁词族之外。

items.meaning: a point, a triangle, an unpaired third
items.meaningCN: 尖角；三角形；落单的第三个

items.meaning: to risk money on an outcome

definition_en: in or to a place that is not named, or about
core_image: 一张摊开的地图上有一个没标名字的小圆点
scene: 我把钥匙放在家里的某个地方了。 I left the keys somewhere in the house.
sceneCN: 这里 somewhere 是「在某处」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我把钥匙放在家里的某个地方了。

senses.title: In some place
senses.definition: in or to a place that is not named or not known
senses.definitionCN: 在或去一个没有说明或不认识的地方
senses.example: I left the keys somewhere in the house.
senses.exampleCN: 我把钥匙放在家里的某个地方了。
senses.why: Some plus where names a place while leaving it blank.
senses.whyCN: some 加 where，指一个地方，却把位置留空。

senses.title: About
senses.definition: used before a number to mean about
senses.definitionCN: 用于数字前表示大约
senses.example: The cost was somewhere around fifty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 费用大约是五十英镑。
senses.why: An unnamed point becomes an approximate point.
senses.whyCN: 未说明的位置变成了近似的位置。

intro.en: Somewhere joins some with the old word where.
intro.cn: somewhere 把 some 与古老的 where 组合在一起。

items.en: Sum meant some; hwær meant where.
items.cn: sum 意为一些，hwær 意为哪里。

items.en: The compound named an unstated place.
items.cn: 这个复合词指未说明的地点。

items.en: It became the everyday adverb for unknown places.
items.cn: 它成为表示未知地点的日常副词。

items.en: It also came to mean about, before numbers.
items.cn: 它也开始在数字前表示大约。

items.en: Get somewhere grew to mean make progress.
items.cn: get somewhere 逐渐表示「有所进展」。

note.en: Somewhere is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of place.
note.cn: 把 somewhere 与形近词以及表示地点的副词作比较。

entries.definition: in some way
on some occasions
a little
in any place
in another place
approximately

normalIntro.en: Somewhere points at a place without writing the address.
normalIntro.cn: somewhere 指向一个地方，却不写地址。

normal.en: I left the keys somewhere in the house.
normal.cn: 我把钥匙放在家里的某个地方了。

normal.en: The cost was somewhere around fifty pounds.
normal.cn: 费用大约是五十英镑。

normal.en: Let us meet somewhere quiet.
normal.cn: 我们找个安静的地方见面吧。

normal.en: She lives somewhere near the river.
normal.cn: 她住在河附近的某个地方。

normal.en: At last the project is getting somewhere.
normal.cn: 这个项目终于有进展了。

abstract.en: Somewhere is a place kept ready for a name.
abstract.cn: somewhere 是一个为名字留着的地方。

abstract.en: Not knowing where is still knowing there is a where.
abstract.cn: 不知道在哪里，仍然知道「有一个地方」。

abstract.en: Every map begins with somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每一张地图都从「某个地方」开始。

examples.en: I left the keys somewhere in the house.
examples.cn: 我把钥匙放在家里的某个地方了。

examples.en: Let us meet somewhere quiet.
examples.cn: 我们找个安静的地方见面吧。

examples.en: At last the project is getting somewhere.
examples.cn: 这个项目终于有进展了。

dict_mnemonic.text: somewhere 就是 some（某个）加 where（哪里）：某个还不知道的地方；somewhere else 是「别处」，somewhere around 是「大约」，get somewhere 是「有进展」。

root: 由 some（某个）与 where（哪里）组合而成，核心义「某个未说明的地点」。

sensesIntro.en: Somewhere means in or to an unnamed place, or about before a number.
sensesIntro.cn: somewhere 意为在或去某个未说明的地方，或在数字前表示大约。

core.en: A place held in mind without an address.
core.cn: 心里有、却没有地址的地方。

branches.en: Keys hide in a room already searched.
branches.cn: 钥匙藏在已经找过的房间里。

branches.en: A price lands near fifty pounds.
branches.cn: 价格落在五十英镑附近。

branches.en: A place and a number can both be approximate.
branches.cn: 地点和数字都可以是近似的。

branches.en: Somewhere else moves the blank to a new place.
branches.cn: somewhere else 把空白移到了另一个地方。

branches.en: Approximate points still point somewhere.
branches.cn: 近似的点，仍然指向某个地方。

intro.en: Somewhere belongs to the some- family of unnamed places.
intro.cn: somewhere 属于由 some 构成、表示未知地点的词族。

latinIntro.en: Somewhere has no Latin root; both parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: somewhere 没有拉丁词根，两部分都来自古英语。

items.example: The bus was nowhere in sight.
items.exampleCN: 公交车连影子都看不见。

definition_zh: 卡车；运货汽车；铁路平板车
definition_en: a large road vehicle built for carrying goods; in Britain it is the usual word for a truck
core_image: 一辆方正的运货车停在仓库门口，后厢里堆满纸箱
scene: 清晨的仓库门口，一辆辆运货的重型车排成长队，等着卸下昨夜的货物。 A lorry loaded with boxes waited at the gate while the workers checked the list.
sceneCN: 这里 lorry 是「卡车、运货汽车」（第 1 个义项）；句意为一辆装满箱子的卡车停在门口，工人核对清单。画面里可认出仓库门、纸箱和清单。

senses.title: A large motor vehicle for carrying goods
senses.definition: a large motor vehicle with an open or enclosed body, built to carry goods on roads
senses.definitionCN: 带有敞篷或封闭车厢、在公路上运送货物的大型机动车辆
senses.example: The lorry carried furniture from the warehouse to the new flat.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆卡车把家具从仓库运到新公寓。
senses.why: When motor vehicles replaced horse carts, the old word for a goods cart was kept for the new machine that did the same job.
senses.whyCN: 当机动车取代马拉车时，原本指运货车的老词被保留下来，用来指干同样工作的新机器。

senses.title: A railway wagon for goods
senses.definition: a flat or open railway wagon used for carrying goods or materials
senses.definitionCN: 用于运送货物或材料的平板或敞篷铁路车皮
senses.example: The coal was loaded onto a lorry waiting on the sidings.
senses.exampleCN: 煤被装上停在侧线的铁路平板车。
senses.why: Before the motor lorry, the same word named the rail wagon that hauled goods inside mines and yards.
senses.whyCN: 在机动车出现之前，同一个词就指矿井和堆场里牵引货物的铁路车皮。

senses.title: A low flat cart, in older British use
senses.definition: a low, flat cart without high sides, used in earlier British English for moving heavy loads
senses.definitionCN: 早期英式英语中指没有高栏、用来搬运重物的低平板车
senses.example: In the old prints, a lorry stands beside the dock with barrels piled on it.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧版画里，一辆低平板车停在码头边，上面堆着木桶。
senses.why: The earliest lorry was simply a low platform on wheels, and that flat shape is where the modern word began.
senses.whyCN: 最早的 lorry 不过是带轮子的低平台，现代这个词正是从那种平板形状开始的。

intro.en: The origin of lorry is uncertain; most accounts trace it to an old British dialect word for dragging or hauling.
intro.cn: lorry 的来源不确定；多数说法把它追溯到古英语方言中表示「拖、拽」的词。

items.en: Lorry first appears in print in the early nineteenth century, naming a low flat cart or wagon.
items.cn: lorry 在十九世纪初首次见于书面记录，指低平板车或货车。

items.en: One common view derives it from dialect lurry, to drag or pull with effort; the source is not certain.
items.cn: 一种常见看法认为它来自方言词 lurry，意为费力地拖拽；但来源并不确定。

items.en: In the railway age lorry named an open goods wagon running on rails.
items.cn: 在铁路时代，lorry 指在轨道上运行的敞篷货车皮。

items.en: When motor vehicles took over, British English moved the word to the road and used it for a motor truck.
items.cn: 当机动车接管运输后，英式英语把这个词移到公路上，用来指机动卡车。

items.en: Today lorry is the everyday British word for a truck, while American English prefers truck.
items.cn: 今天 lorry 是英式英语里指卡车的日常词，而美式英语更常用 truck。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words easily confused with lorry in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group collects other goods vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组收在拼写或读音上容易与 lorry 混淆的词；近义组收其他运货车辆。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and opaque, so its memory hooks come from its British identity, its railway past and its place among goods vehicles.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短而难以拆分，所以记忆钩子来自它的英式身份、铁路渊源以及它在运货车辆中的位置。

normal.en: Lorry is the everyday British word for a truck, so remembering the country helps fix the meaning.
normal.cn: lorry 是英式英语里指卡车的日常词，记住它属于英国就能固定词义。

normal.en: Its plural is lorries, because the final y turns to ies after a consonant.
normal.cn: 它的复数是 lorries，因为辅音后的 y 要变成 ies。

normal.en: The word first named a low cart and later a railway wagon, so it moved from rails to roads.
normal.cn: 这个词先指低平板车，后指铁路车皮，因此是从铁轨走向公路。

normal.en: Lorry driver and lorry park are fixed British compounds, which keep the word in daily transport talk.
normal.cn: lorry driver 与 lorry park 是固定的英式复合词，让这个词留在日常运输话题里。

normal.en: A heavy lorry takes a wide lane, which is why the word often appears in road rules.
normal.cn: 重型卡车要占很宽的车道，所以这个词常出现在交通规则里。

abstract.en: A word for a cart on rails becoming the word for a truck shows how transport words follow the machine, not the road.
abstract.cn: 一个指铁轨上货车的词变成指卡车的词，说明交通词汇跟着机器走，而不是跟着路面走。

abstract.en: Lorry and truck name the same thing in two countries, a reminder that synonyms can be national habits.
abstract.cn: lorry 与 truck 在两个国家指同一事物，提醒人近义词也可以是国民习惯。

abstract.en: The flat platform at the start of lorry is still visible in its boxy shape today.
abstract.cn: lorry 起点处的平板形状，今天仍能在它方方正正的车身上看见。

senses.title: The spirit of a person

intro.en: Soul is an old Germanic word for the life within a person.
intro.cn: soul 是一个古老的日耳曼词，指人内在的生命。

items.en: Sawol meant the spirit or life of a person.
items.cn: sawol 意为人的灵魂或生命。

items.en: The form became soule and kept the sacred sense.
items.cn: 词形变为 soule，保留了神圣的含义。

items.en: It came to mean the deep feeling inside a person.
items.cn: 它开始表示人内心深处的感情。

items.en: The word also named a living person, as in not a soul.
items.cn: 这个词也用来指活人，如 not a soul（一个人也没有）。

items.en: In the twentieth century it named a style of music.

senses.definitionCN: 涂有磁性材料、可存储声音或影像的长条
senses.example: The old tape still plays in his car.
senses.exampleCN: 那盘旧磁带还能在他的车里播放。
senses.why: A thin strip became the carrier of recorded sound.
senses.whyCN: 细长的带子变成录制声音的载体。

senses.title: To stick with tape
senses.definition: to fix something in place with sticky tape
senses.definitionCN: 用黏胶带把东西固定住
senses.example: He taped the note to the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他用胶带把便条贴在门上。
senses.why: The noun turned into the act of applying it.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转化为「贴上胶带」的动作。

senses.title: To record sound or pictures
senses.definition: to record something on tape or a digital medium
senses.definitionCN: 把声音或画面录制下来
senses.example: They taped the interview for the radio.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为电台录制了这次采访。
senses.why: Recording put sound onto the moving strip, so the strip gave its name to the act.
senses.whyCN: 录制是把声音存到移动的带子上，于是带名成了动作名。

intro.en: Tape first meant a narrow woven band, long before glue or music.
intro.cn: tape 最初指窄织带，远早于胶与录音。

items.en: Tæppe meant a narrow strip of cloth.
items.cn: tæppe 意为窄布带。

items.en: Tape kept the sense of a thin band.
items.cn: tape 保留了细带之义。

items.en: Adhesive tape gave the strip a new use.

items.en: Magnetic tape carried recorded sound.
items.cn: 磁带承载录制的声音。

items.en: The verb means to stick or to record.

senses.title: Undergo

definition_zh: 购物中心；林荫道；步行商业街
definition_en: a large shopping centre, originally a shaded walk or tree-lined promenade, and later a street given over to shops and pedestrians
core_image: 玻璃幕墙围起的长廊，两侧店铺灯火通明，人流沿中央通道向前
scene: 周末下午，自动门一开，冷气裹着爆米花的味道涌出来。 On Saturday afternoon the mall was so crowded that we parked two blocks away.
sceneCN: 这里是「购物中心」（第 1 个义项：大型商场）；句意为周六下午商场挤得只能把车停在两个街区外。

pos.zh: 购物中心；林荫道；步行商业街

derivatives.zh: 由 mall 与 rat 复合，口语中指常年在商场闲逛的年轻人
由 mall 与 goer 复合，义为「常去商场的人」
由前缀 mega-（巨大）加 mall 构成，义为「超大型购物中心」

senses.title: A large enclosed shopping centre
senses.definition: a large building or covered area containing many shops, restaurants and places of entertainment
senses.definitionCN: 包含许多商店、餐厅和娱乐场所的大型建筑或有顶区域
senses.example: The new mall has a cinema and a food court on the top floor.
senses.exampleCN: 新商场顶层有电影院和美食广场。
senses.why: The long covered walk of the old game alley was rebuilt as a corridor of shops, so the promenade turned into a shopping centre.
senses.whyCN: 旧日球场那条有顶的长廊被改建成一条店铺走廊，散步的长道于是变成了购物中心。

senses.title: A tree-lined walk or promenade
senses.definition: a shaded walk or public promenade, especially one planted with trees
senses.definitionCN: 有遮阴的步道或公共散步场所，尤指两旁种树的
senses.example: Couples strolled along the mall in the afternoon shade.
senses.exampleCN: 午后树荫下，情侣们沿着林荫道散步。
senses.why: The name began with a long alley for a ball game, and any broad walk shaded by trees borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字最初指一条打槌球的长场地，后来任何有树荫的宽阔步道都借用了同一个词。

senses.title: A street set aside for pedestrians and shops
senses.definition: a street closed to traffic and lined with shops, common in American town centres
senses.definitionCN: 禁止车辆通行、两旁布满店铺的街道，常见于美国城镇中心
senses.example: The old main street became a mall after the cars were banned.
senses.exampleCN: 禁止汽车通行之后，那条老街变成了步行商业街。
senses.why: When a town closes a street to cars and hands it to shops, the old promenade sense widens into a business street.
senses.whyCN: 当一座城镇把街道对汽车关闭、交给店铺使用时，原本「散步长道」的词义就扩展成商业街道。

intro.en: Mall is usually traced through the game pall-mall, a long alley for ball and mallet, before it named a shaded walk and then a shopping centre.
intro.cn: mall 一般认为经由槌球游戏 pall-mall（用球与木槌、在长场地上进行的游戏）演变而来，先指有荫的长道，后指购物中心。

items.en: The route from the game to the modern word is reconstructed rather than documented, and dictionaries mark parts of it as uncertain.
items.cn: 从这种游戏到现代词义的路径多为重构，而非有明确文献记载，词典也把其中部分环节标为来源不确定。

items.en: Italian pallamaglio joined palla, a ball, with maglio, a mallet, and both words go back to Latin palla and malleus.
items.cn: 意大利语 pallamaglio 把表示球的 palla 与表示木槌的 maglio 组合起来，二者都可追溯到拉丁语 palla 与 malleus。

items.en: French took the game as pallemaille and passed the form to English in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这项游戏称作 pallemaille，并在十七世纪把这个形式传给英语。

items.en: Pall-mall named both the game and the long alley where it was played, including the London walk that became The Mall.
items.cn: pall-mall 既指这项游戏，也指打球的长场地，其中包括后来称为 The Mall 的伦敦那条大道。

items.en: By the twentieth century mall meant a shaded walk and then, above all in North America, an enclosed shopping centre.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，mall 先指有荫的步道，随后尤其在北美指有顶的购物中心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the old game and on mall itself; the near-meaning group gathers words for shopping spaces and promenades.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在旧日游戏与 mall 本身之上的形式；近义组收表示购物场所与散步长道的词。

entries.definition: The old ball-and-mallet game and the alley where it was played.
entries.definitionCN: 旧日的球与木槌游戏，以及打球的长场地。

entries.definition: A young person who spends a lot of time in shopping malls.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间泡在商场里的年轻人。

entries.definition: An extremely large shopping mall.
A tree-lined promenade in London, named after the old game alley.
entries.definitionCN: 伦敦的一条林荫大道，得名于旧日的球场长道。

entries.definition: A group of shops built together under one management.
entries.definitionCN: 集中建造、统一经营的一组商店。

entries.definition: A public square or a small group of shops around it.
entries.definitionCN: 公共广场，或其周围的一小片商店。

entries.definition: A covered passage with shops along both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 两侧有店铺的有顶通道。

entries.definition: A broad public walk, especially one beside the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 宽阔的公共散步道，尤指海滨的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the name of a game alley, kept the shape of a long walk, and finally filled that shape with shops.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一条球场长道的名字，保留了长条形步道的形状，最后又在这个形状里填满店铺。

normal.en: Mall and pall-mall share one history: a ball, a mallet, and a long alley to play in.
normal.cn: mall 与 pall-mall 共用一段历史：一只球、一把木槌，还有一条打球的长场地。

normal.en: The Mall in London was a promenade before it was a name on a map, and the shopping sense came much later.
normal.cn: 伦敦的 The Mall 先是散步大道，后来才成为地图上的名字，购物义出现得更晚。

normal.en: Strip mall describes shops in a line beside a car park, the opposite of the enclosed mall.
normal.cn: strip mall 指停车场旁排成一线的店铺，与有顶的 mall 正好相反。

normal.en: Megamall simply adds mega, great, to mall, so the compound says the size twice.
normal.cn: megamall 只是把表示「巨大」的 mega 加到 mall 上，等于把尺寸说了两遍。

normal.en: Mall rat is informal for a young person who spends hours in a mall, built like bookworm and couch potato.
normal.cn: mall rat 是口语说法，指在商场里一待就是几小时的年轻人，构词方式类似 bookworm 与 couch potato。

abstract.en: A row of trees over a gravel path and a row of shop windows under one roof are the same long corridor, centuries apart.
abstract.cn: 碎石小径上的一排树，与同一屋顶下的一排橱窗，是同一条长廊，只是隔了几个世纪。

abstract.en: A ball game vanished, but the alley where it was played survives in the name of a shopping hall.
abstract.cn: 球戏消失了，但打球的那条长场地以购物大厅之名的形式留存下来。

abstract.en: The word lost its game, kept its shape, and filled the shape with shops.
abstract.cn: 这个词丢掉了游戏，保留了形状，又在这个形状里装满了店铺。

examples.en: The new mall has a cinema on the top floor.
examples.cn: 新商场顶层有一家电影院。

examples.en: Couples strolled along the mall in the afternoon shade.
examples.cn: 午后树荫下，情侣们沿着林荫道散步。

examples.en: The old main street became a mall after the cars were banned.
examples.cn: 禁止汽车通行之后，那条老街变成了步行商业街。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩尔」——摩尔商场里人潮涌动，走廊长得望不到头；记住 mall 是购物中心。

root: 一般认为源出意大利语 pallamaglio（球与木槌的游戏），经法语 pallemaille 进入英语作 pall-mall；词源路径多为重构，无可靠拉丁同族词直接对应。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a long shaded corridor for walking; the word then names a pedestrian shopping street and, finally, a large enclosed shopping centre.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一条有荫的狭长通道；词义由此指步行商业街，最后指有顶的大型购物中心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long glass-roofed corridor with shops on both sides and people walking down the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条玻璃顶的长廊，两侧是店铺，人流沿中央向前走。

branches.en: a glass door sliding open into cold air and bright lights
branches.cn: 玻璃门滑开，涌出冷气与灯光

branches.en: a row of trees over a gravel path
branches.cn: 碎石小径上的一排树

branches.en: a street closed to cars and handed to walkers
branches.cn: 禁止汽车通行、交给行人的街

branches.en: a covered walk that turned into a hall of shops
branches.cn: 从有顶步道变成的商铺大厅

branches.en: an old name still printed on a city map
branches.cn: 旧名字仍印在城市地图上

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin ball and mallet behind the Italian game, the French and English reshapings, and English compounds built on mall.
intro.cn: 这个词由意大利语游戏背后的拉丁语「球」与「木槌」、法语与英语的改写形式，以及建立在 mall 上的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin survives here at two removes: palla gave the ball and malleus gave the mallet in the Italian game that English took over as pall-mall.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这里隔了两层留存：palla 给出「球」，malleus 给出「木槌」，共同构成英语接手的那项意大利游戏 pall-mall。

items.meaning: a game played with a ball and a mallet

items.meaning: the same game in French form

definition_en: a scientist who studies chemistry, or a person who prepares and sells medicines
core_image: 穿白大褂在药柜前配药的人
scene: 街角那家小店的招牌已经褪色。 The chemist weighed the powder and sealed it in a small bottle.
sceneCN: 这里 chemist 指「药剂师」（第 2 个义项：配制并出售药物的人）；句意是药剂师称好药粉，封进一只小瓶。

senses.title: A chemistry scientist
senses.definition: a scientist who studies the composition and behaviour of substances
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质组成与变化规律的科学家
senses.example: The chemist published a paper on new polymers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位化学家发表了一篇关于新型聚合物的论文。
senses.why: The -ist ending marks a person who practises the science named by the stem.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 标记出从事词干所命名那门科学的人。

senses.title: A person who sells medicines
senses.definition: a person trained to prepare and sell medicines in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、在店铺里配制并出售药物的人
senses.example: Ask the chemist before mixing these pills.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些药混着吃之前先问药剂师。
senses.why: In Britain the same trained person both studies drugs and hands them over the counter.
senses.whyCN: 在英国，同一位受过训练的人既研究药物，也在柜台后把药交给顾客。

senses.title: A shop selling medicines
senses.definition: a shop where medicines and small health goods are sold
senses.definitionCN: 出售药物与小型保健用品的店铺
senses.example: The chemist opens at eight on weekdays.
senses.exampleCN: 这家药房工作日八点开门。
senses.why: British speech shortens the chemist's shop to the chemist, so the person's name becomes the place.
senses.whyCN: 英式口语把 the chemist's shop 缩成 the chemist，人的称呼便成了地点。

intro.en: Chemist came from the same alchemy root that gave chemical and chemistry.
intro.cn: chemist 与 chemical、chemistry 同出炼金术这一词根。

items.en: Khemeia named the art of transforming metals.
items.cn: 希腊语 khemeia 指转化金属的技艺。

items.en: Al-kimiya carried the art into Arabic.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-kimiya 把这门技艺带入阿拉伯语。

items.en: Alchimia named the art, and alchimista named its follower.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchimia 指这门技艺，alchimista 指从事者。

items.en: Chemist first meant a student of this art.
items.cn: chemist 最初指这门技艺的研习者。

items.en: The word split into the scientist and the medicine seller.
items.cn: 这个词分化出科学家与卖药人两个意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the chem- stem, while the meaning group names people who handle medicines.
note.cn: 形近组共享 chem- 词干，近义组列出与药物打交道的人。

entries.definition: relating to chemistry
the science of substances
a follower of the old art of alchemy
a person trained to prepare medicines
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练配制药物的人

entries.definition: an American word for a medicine seller
an old word for a person who sold medicines

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ist person ending, the British shop idiom and the shared chem- stem.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用表示人的 -ist 词尾、英式店铺说法以及共同的 chem- 词干。

normal.en: Add -ist to chem and you get the person: a chemist works with chemistry.
normal.cn: 在 chem 后加 -ist 就得到那个人：chemist 与 chemistry 打交道。

normal.en: In Britain the chemist is both the scientist and the shop on the corner.
normal.cn: 在英国，chemist 既是科学家，也是街角那家药房。

normal.en: The chemist's means the shop, with the apostrophe standing for the missing word shop.
normal.cn: the chemist's 指那家店，撇号代替了省略掉的 shop 一词。

normal.en: Chemistry is the subject, chemist is the person, chemical is the adjective.
normal.cn: chemistry 是学科，chemist 是人，chemical 是形容词。

normal.en: An alchemist came first; a chemist is the modern heir of that old figure.
normal.cn: 先有 alchemist，chemist 是那位古老人物在现代的继承者。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat behind a counter of small drawers.
abstract.cn: 想象白色工作服站在一排小抽屉的柜台后。

abstract.en: Picture a hand weighing white powder on a brass scale.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在铜秤上称白色粉末。

abstract.en: Picture a hand-written label being pressed onto a brown bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象一张手写标签被贴到棕色瓶子上。

examples.en: The chemist explained how the two drugs interact.
examples.cn: 药剂师解释了这两种药如何相互作用。

examples.en: She trained as a chemist before turning to teaching.
examples.cn: 她在转行教书之前受训成为化学家。

examples.en: I bought the bandage at the chemist's on the corner.
examples.cn: 我在街角那家药房买了绷带。

dict_mnemonic.text: chem 加 -ist：跟化学打交道的人，既是化学家，也是给人配药的药剂师。

root: 源自希腊语 khemeia（转化金属之术），经阿拉伯语 al-kimiya、中世纪拉丁语 alchimista 进入英语，-ist 表示从事者。

sensesIntro.en: One trained person gives all three senses: the researcher, the dispenser and the shop where the dispenser works.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一位受过训练的人给出三个义项：研究者、配药者，以及配药者工作的店铺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trained hand measuring powder behind a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台后一只称量药粉的熟练的手。

branches.en: The scientist sense keeps the laboratory.
branches.cn: 科学家义项保留实验室场景。

branches.en: The dispenser sense moves to the counter.
branches.cn: 配药者义项转到柜台前。

branches.en: The shop sense names the place itself.
branches.cn: 店铺义项指地点本身。

branches.en: Both senses need the same chemical training.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要同样的化学训练。

branches.en: The person's name stands for the shop in British speech.
branches.cn: 在英式口语中，人的称呼代指那家店。

intro.en: Chemist is the chem- stem plus the person ending -ist.
intro.cn: chemist 是 chem- 词干加上表示人的词尾 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin alchimista, a follower of alchimia, is the direct model for chemist.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alchimista 是 chemist 的直接范本，指炼金术的从事者。

items.meaning: a scientist or a medicine seller

items.exampleCN: 两位化学家签署了报告。

definition_zh: 评估；评定；评价；教育测评；核定（税额）；评估结果
definition_en: the act of judging the value, quality, or amount of something, a formal judgement, a test of learning, or a tax fixed by authority
core_image: 一叠批改过的作文与一支红笔，旁边写着定好的分数
scene: 学期末的办公桌上摊着一摞作文，红笔在每页的分数栏里落下数字。 The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 assessment 是「评估、评定」（第 1 个义项：判断价值或质量的行为）；句意为「每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟」。画面中有摊开的作文、红笔与分数栏。

pos.zh: 名词：评估；评定；评价；教育测评；核定税额；评估结果

derivatives.zh: assessment 的动词形式，义为「评估；评定；核定」
由 assess 加 -or 构成，义为「评估员；估税员」
由 assess 加 -able 构成，义为「可评估的；可征税的」
由前缀 re- 加 assessment 构成，义为「重新评估」

senses.title: The act of judging value or quality
senses.definition: the act of judging or estimating the value, quality, or seriousness of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断或估算某物的价值、质量或严重程度的行为
senses.example: The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟。
senses.why: -ment turns the verb assess into the action itself: the sitting-beside and weighing is now a named event.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词 assess 变成动作本身：那场「坐在旁边称一称」如今成了一个有名字的事件。

senses.title: A test of learning
senses.definition: a formal test or judgement of a pupil's progress, often spread over a course
senses.definitionCN: 对学生学习进展的正式测评，常贯穿整个课程
senses.example: The course uses continuous assessment instead of one final exam.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课采用持续性评价，而不是一次期末考试。
senses.why: If weighing a pupil's work is assess, then the whole system of weighing is an assessment.
senses.whyCN: 如果评一份作业是 assess，那么整套称量的制度就是 assessment。

senses.title: A tax fixed by authority
senses.definition: an official calculation of the tax or fine owed by a person or property
senses.definitionCN: 对个人或财产应缴税款、罚金的官方计算
senses.example: The tax assessment arrived with the winter bill.
senses.exampleCN: 税额核定单随冬季账单一起寄到。
senses.why: This is the oldest official use: an assessor sits beside the property and names the sum.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的官方用法：估税员坐在产业旁边，报出一个数目。

senses.title: The judgement reached
senses.definition: the opinion or rating that results from assessing something
senses.definitionCN: 评估某物之后得出的意见或评级
senses.example: Her assessment was that the plan needed more time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的评价是这个计划还需要更多时间。
senses.why: By shifting from the act to its result, an assessment becomes the verdict someone has reached.
senses.whyCN: 由行为转指结果，assessment 便成了某人得出的结论。

intro.en: Assessment is the noun of assess, and both keep the Latin image of an official sitting beside a property to fix its value.
intro.cn: assessment 是 assess 的名词，两者都保留着「官员坐在产业旁边核定价值」这一拉丁意象。

items.en: The root 「*sed-」 meant 'to sit', and it lies behind many Latin words for sitting and settling.
items.cn: 词根「*sed-」意为「坐」，拉丁语中许多表示坐与安顿的词都由它而来。

items.en: Assidere meant 'to sit beside', from ad- 'to' plus sedere 'to sit'.
items.cn: assidere 意为「坐在旁边」，由 ad-「向」加 sedere「坐」构成。

items.en: An assessor sat beside a magistrate to fix taxes and fines.
items.cn: assessor 坐在长官旁边，协助核定税额与罚金。

items.en: Assesser carried the verb into French with the sense of fixing what is owed.
items.cn: 古法语 assesser 把这个动词带进法语，意思是核定应缴数额。

items.en: English assess began with taxes, and assessment followed as its noun.
items.cn: 英语的 assess 先用于税务，assessment 随后作为它的名词出现。

items.en: Education gave the word a large new field: continuous assessment now weighs pupils, not property.
items.cn: 教育为这个词开辟了大片新领域：持续性评价如今称量的是学生，而非产业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns close to assessment in form; the near-meaning group gathers evaluations, appraisals and reviews.
note.cn: 形近组收形式上与 assessment 接近的名词；近义组收评估、鉴定与复查。

entries.definition: A person who assesses, especially one who values property for tax.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「评估员、估税员」。

entries.definition: A part cut off from a whole.
A confident statement that something is true.
A careful judgement of value or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值或质量的仔细判断。

entries.definition: A judgement of worth, often of property or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值的评估，常指房产或表现。

entries.definition: An opinion or decision formed after thought.
entries.definitionCN: 经过思考后形成的意见或决定。

entries.definition: An examination of something to judge its state or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 为判断状况或质量而进行的检查。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from marked essays to a school report, a tax notice and a spoken verdict.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从批改过的作文，走到成绩报告、税单与一句口头结论。

normal.en: Assessment is assess turned into a named event.
normal.cn: assessment 是把 assess 变成一个有名有姓的事件。

normal.en: An assessment of essays: each one is weighed.
normal.cn: 作文评估：每一篇都过一回秤。

normal.en: Continuous assessment: the weighing never stops.
normal.cn: 持续性评价：称量一直没停。

normal.en: A tax assessment: the property is weighed for what it owes.
normal.cn: 税额核定：产业被称一称，看它该缴多少。

normal.en: Her assessment was a verdict in one sentence.
normal.cn: 她的一句评价就是最终结论。

abstract.en: The noun names the act and then the verdict.
abstract.cn: 这个名词先指动作，再指结论。

abstract.en: Tax and school both use the same scale.
abstract.cn: 税务与学校用的是同一架天平。

abstract.en: Every assessment needs a standard to weigh against.
abstract.cn: 任何评估都需要一个可比照的标准。

examples.en: The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
examples.cn: 每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟。

examples.en: The course uses continuous assessment instead of one final exam.
examples.cn: 这门课采用持续性评价，而不是一次期末考试。

examples.en: Her assessment was that the plan needed more time.
examples.cn: 她的评价是这个计划还需要更多时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿塞斯门」——阿塞斯门坐在办公桌前，把每份作业都称一称、打个分：评估

root: assessment 是 assess 加名词后缀 -ment。assess 来自拉丁语 assidere「坐在旁边」，由 ad-「向」与 sedere「坐」构成；assessor 原是坐在长官旁边核定税额的官员。因此 assessment 先指「核定应缴数额」这一官方行为，后泛指判断价值、质量、风险的行为，再指教育中的测评制度，最后由行为转指得出的评价与结论。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses grow from one weighing: the act of judging, a course-wide test of learning, an official tax sum, and the verdict reached.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从同一次称量长出来：判断的行为、贯穿课程的测评、官方核定的税额，以及最终得出的结论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of marked essays beside a red pen and a column of scores.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠批改过的作文，旁边是一支红笔与一列分数。

branches.en: THE WEIGHING LINE: judging value or quality is the core act.
branches.cn: 称量线：判断价值或质量是核心动作。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: the weighing becomes a course-long system.
branches.cn: 学校线：称量变成贯穿课程的制度。

branches.en: THE TAX LINE: an official fixes what a property owes.
branches.cn: 税务线：官员定下产业该缴多少。

branches.en: THE VERDICT LINE: the act turns into the opinion reached.
branches.cn: 结论线：动作转成得出的意见。

branches.en: THE REPORT LINE: a written assessment records both the act and the verdict.
branches.cn: 报告线：书面评估同时记录动作与结论。

intro.en: Assessment is assess plus -ment; its family adds -or, -able and the prefix re-.
intro.cn: assessment 是 assess 加 -ment，词族再加 -or、-able 与前缀 re-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root sedere 'to sit' also gave assessor and sedentary, keeping the image of sitting beside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 sedere「坐」还生出 assessor 与 sedentary，保留着「坐在旁边」的形象。

items.meaning: the act or result of judging
items.example: The assessment was fair to both sides.
items.exampleCN: 这项评估对双方都算公道。

items.example: The school holds two assessments each term.
items.exampleCN: 学校每学期进行两次测评。

items.meaning: to judge or fix a value
items.example: We assess the risk before every flight.
items.exampleCN: 每次飞行前我们都会评估风险。

items.meaning: able to be assessed or taxed
items.example: The gift is not assessable income.
items.exampleCN: 这笔赠与不属于应税收入。

items.example: The city reassessed the flood risk.
items.exampleCN: 城市重新评估了洪水风险。

items.meaning: judging one's own work or tax
items.meaningCN: 自我评估；自行申报纳税
items.example: Self-assessment saves the office a visit.
items.exampleCN: 自行申报省得跑一趟税务局。

latinEntries.meaning: one who sits beside to judge
latinEntries.meaningCN: 坐在旁边协助判断的人
latinEntries.example: The assessor set the fine at ten pounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 估税员把罚金定为十英镑。

latinEntries.example: A sedentary life weakens the legs.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 久坐的生活会让腿变弱。

definition_zh: 最终的；最后的；根本的；极致的；最好的
definition_en: last in a series or process, or greatest, most extreme and most basic of its kind
core_image: 长队排到尽头的那一位，也是压轴出场的最强者
scene: 十年施工的隧道终于全线贯通，剪彩仪式定在最末一日举行。 The bridge opening was the ultimate event of the decade-long project.
sceneCN: 这里 ultimate 是形容词「最终的、最后的」（第 1 个义项：序列或过程的末位）；句意为通车典礼是这个长达十年工程的收官大事。

pos.zh: 形容词：最终的；最后的；根本的；极致的
名词：终极；顶点（常用于 the ultimate in ...）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「最终；根本上」
同族拉丁词经借入，义为「最后通牒」
加表示「几乎」的前缀构成，义为「倒数第二的」

senses.title: Last in a series or process
senses.definition: happening or coming at the end of a long series or process
senses.definitionCN: 发生在漫长序列或过程的末尾
senses.example: The merger was the ultimate step in a decade of cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并是十年合作的最后一步。
senses.why: The Latin source meant simply the last one; the queue's final member is the ultimate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原义就是「最后一个」；队列尽头的那位即是 ultimate。

senses.title: Most extreme or greatest of its kind
senses.definition: the greatest, best or most extreme example of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类中最好、最强或最极端的例子
senses.example: This car is the ultimate driving machine of its era.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车是那个时代的终极座驾。
senses.why: If nothing comes after the last, the last is also the peak; the end of the line doubles as the top.
senses.whyCN: 既然「最后」之后不再有，末位同时也就是顶点。

senses.title: Fundamental or basic
senses.definition: most basic or fundamental, as of causes, principles or realities
senses.definitionCN: 就原因、原则或现实而言，最为根本
senses.example: Physicists still search for the ultimate nature of matter.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家仍在探寻物质的根本性质。
senses.why: Dig beneath the layers and the deepest layer is the last one; fundamental equals final.
senses.whyCN: 层层剥开，最深层就是最后一层；「根本」与「最终」在此重合。

senses.title: Supreme in authority
senses.definition: holding the highest or final authority, as of responsibility or power
senses.definitionCN: 就责任或权力而言，拥有最高或最终决定权
senses.example: The board bears ultimate responsibility for the fund.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会为该基金承担最终责任。
senses.why: Authority also forms a chain; where it stops is where it is ultimate.
senses.whyCN: 权力也构成链条；链条终止之处即为最高。

senses.title: The ultimate sacrifice
senses.definition: in the phrase the ultimate sacrifice, the giving of one's life for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 the ultimate sacrifice，指为事业献出生命
senses.example: The memorial honours those who paid the ultimate sacrifice.
senses.exampleCN: 纪念碑缅怀那些献出生命的人。
senses.why: Life is the last thing a person can give; nothing stands behind it.
senses.whyCN: 生命是一个人所能给出的最后之物；它背后再无可给。

senses.title: The ultimate in something
senses.definition: as a noun, the finest or most extreme degree of a quality, as in the ultimate in luxury
senses.definitionCN: 名词用法，指某种品质的最高或极端程度，如 the ultimate in luxury
senses.example: The spa claims to be the ultimate in relaxation.
senses.exampleCN: 这家水疗中心自称是放松的极致。
senses.why: The adjective is nominalized: the peak itself becomes the thing named.
senses.whyCN: 形容词名词化：顶点本身成为被命名之物。

senses.title: Ultimate cause versus proximate cause
senses.definition: in philosophy and biology, the deepest cause behind an immediate one
senses.definitionCN: 哲学与生物学中，位于直接原因背后的最深层原因
senses.example: Biologists separate the proximate mechanism from the ultimate cause of a behavior.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家把行为的直接机制与其终极原因分开。
senses.why: Causes stack in layers; the question behind the last question is ultimate.
senses.whyCN: 原因层层叠加；最后一个问题背后的问题即终极问题。

senses.title: Ultimatum: the last word in negotiation
senses.definition: in the related noun ultimatum, a final proposal whose rejection ends negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 同族名词 ultimatum 中，指拒绝即终结谈判的最后提案
senses.example: The union issued an ultimatum before striking.
senses.exampleCN: 工会罢工前发出了最后通牒。
senses.why: The family word keeps the Latin sense of the last: nothing comes after it.
senses.whyCN: 同族词保留了拉丁语「最后」之义：其后不再有别的话。

intro.en: Ultimate is the superlative of the Latin word for last, adopted as a learned borrowing.
intro.cn: ultimate 是拉丁语「最后」一词的最高级形式，作为学术借词进入英语。

items.en: *al- is generally reconstructed as 'to grow, nourish'; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *al- 意为「生长、滋养」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin ultimus meant 'farthest, last', the superlative of ulter or the base of ultra 'beyond'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus 意为「最远的、最后的」，是 ulter 的最高级，与 ultra「越过」同基。

items.en: Medieval Latin ultimatus meant 'reduced to the last, final', formed on ultimus.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 ultimatus 意为「至于最后、终结的」，由 ultimus 构成。

items.en: Ecclesiastical Latin used ultimatus for final states, keeping the superlative force.
items.cn: 教会拉丁语用 ultimatus 表示终结状态，保留最高级力度。

items.en: English adopted ultimate in the seventeenth century in learned and legal contexts for the last or furthest.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 ultimate，用于学术与法律语境，指最后、最远。

items.en: Advertising later stretched the word to mean the best of its kind, adding the modern peak sense.
items.cn: 后来的广告用语把它拉伸为「同类最佳」，添出现代的顶点义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin ultimus family; the near-meaning group gathers last, final and supreme words.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 ultimus 词族；近义组收最后、最终与最高级词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning finally or fundamentally.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最终；根本上」，由本词派生。

entries.definition: A final proposal whose rejection ends talks; neuter form of the Latin superlative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「最后通牒」，是该拉丁最高级的中性形式。

entries.definition: Second to last; built with a prefix meaning almost.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「倒数第二的」，加表示「几乎」的前缀构成。

entries.definition: A prefix and word meaning beyond; shares the Latin base with ultimate.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀兼单词，义为「超越」，与本词同出拉丁语词基。

entries.definition: An extreme opinion or practice, from the same Latin base; rare but real.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「极端主义做法」，出自同一拉丁词基，罕见但真实存在。

entries.definition: Coming at the end; neutral and everyday where ultimate sounds learned or grand.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最后的」，日常中性，而 ultimate 听起来更书面、更宏大。

entries.definition: After all others in order; the plainest member of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最后的」，是该义场中最朴素的成员。

entries.definition: Highest in rank or degree; overlaps with the peak sense of ultimate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最高的」，与 ultimate 的顶点义重叠。

entries.definition: Happening at last, after delay; stresses the outcome after time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最终的（经过一段时间后）」，强调时间之后的结果。

entries.definition: Forming the end point, often of a process or journey; technical flavor.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「终点的；晚期的」，带技术色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin superlative and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁最高级词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Latin ultimus is the superlative of last: nothing comes after it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 ultimus 是「最后」的最高级：它后面不再有东西。

normal.en: Ultra and ultimate share one base: beyond, then the farthest point.
normal.cn: ultra 与 ultimate 同基：先「越过」，再到最远点。

normal.en: Ultimate responsibility is the duty that cannot be passed on.
normal.cn: ultimate responsibility 是无法转嫁的责任。

normal.en: The ultimate sacrifice means giving one's life.
normal.cn: the ultimate sacrifice 指献出生命。

normal.en: Penultimate is one step before the ultimate.

abstract.en: Picture a queue so long you walk all day, and one person at its far end.

abstract.en: The last of the line is also the strongest of the line.
abstract.cn: 队尾之人也是队列中的最强者。

abstract.en: Dig through every layer of soil; the bedrock at the bottom is ultimate.
abstract.cn: 把土层挖穿，最底下的基岩就是 ultimate。

examples.en: Reducing waste is the ultimate goal of the new packaging design.
examples.cn: 减少浪费是新包装设计的最终目标。

examples.en: Many call this city the ultimate food destination.
examples.cn: 许多人称这座城市为美食的终极目的地。

examples.en: The captain holds ultimate authority over the ship.
examples.cn: 船长对这艘船拥有最高权威。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥缇默特」——奥秘到提到最后才默然揭晓：最终的

root: 拉丁语 ultimus「最远的、最后的」为 ulter 的最高级，与 ultra「越过」同基；经中世纪拉丁语 ultimatus 与教会用法进入英语；一般认为词基可溯至原始印欧语 *al-「生长、滋养」（重构形式），同族词有 ultimatum、penultimate、ultra 等。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of ultimate all stand at the end of a line: the last step, the peak, the bedrock cause, the top authority, the final gift, the nominalized peak, the deep cause in science, and the family's last word in negotiation.
sensesIntro.cn: ultimate 的八个义项都立于队伍之末：最后一步、顶点、基岩之因、最高权威、最后的给予、名词化的极点、科学中的深层原因，以及谈判桌上词族的最后通牒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue stretches to its farthest end, where the last one stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：队伍伸向最远处，尽头站着最后一位。

branches.en: THE ORDER: the final step and the family's final word in negotiation.
branches.cn: 次序线：最后一步与词族在谈判中的最后一言。

branches.en: THE PEAK: the last doubles as the best, as adjective and as noun.
branches.cn: 顶点线：末位即最佳，形容词与名词两用。

branches.en: THE FOUNDATION: bedrock causes behind every surface layer.
branches.cn: 根基线：一切表层之下的基岩原因。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: the chain of power stops where it is ultimate.
branches.cn: 权威线：权力链条终止于最高处。

branches.en: THE GIFT: life is the last thing one can give.
branches.cn: 给予线：生命是人所能给出的最后之物。

latinIntro.en: Latin ultimus, ultimatus and ultra are all recorded; only the Indo-European base is reconstructed.

definition_en: in a serious way, in earnest, or to a large and worrying degree

sceneCN: 这里 seriously 是「认真地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请认真对待这个问题。

senses.title: In earnest

definition_en: elaborate and decorative, imagined rather than real, or to want something
core_image: 橱窗里一条缀满亮片和蕾丝的连衣裙，精致得不太日常
scene: 她穿了一条别致的连衣裙去参加晚会。 She wore a fancy dress to the party.
sceneCN: 这里 fancy 是「别致的；花哨的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她穿了一条别致的连衣裙去参加晚会。

senses.title: Elaborate and decorative
senses.definition: unusually elaborate, decorated, or complicated
senses.definitionCN: 不同寻常地精致、装饰繁复或复杂的
senses.example: The cake had fancy decorations.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋糕上有精致的装饰。
senses.why: The core sense is more decoration than necessary.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是超出必要的装饰。

senses.title: Expensive and upscale
senses.definition: of high quality and cost, often too expensive for everyday use
senses.definitionCN: 质量与价格都高，常超出日常所需
senses.example: They ate at a fancy hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一家高档酒店用餐。

senses.whyCN: 精致成为奢华的标志。

senses.title: Imagination

senses.definitionCN: 想象事物的能力，或想象出的东西
senses.example: The story is a product of fancy.

senses.why: Decoration and imagination both go beyond plain fact.
senses.whyCN: 装饰与想象都超出平淡的事实。

senses.title: Want or like

senses.example: Do you fancy a cup of tea?

senses.why: A passing wish is a fancy in motion.

intro.en: Fancy is a shortened form of fantasy, from Greek phantasia, imagination.
intro.cn: fancy 是 fantasy 的缩略形式，源自希腊语 phantasia（想象）。

items.en: Phantasia meant appearance or imagination.

items.en: Phantasia meant imagination or a phantom.
items.cn: phantasia 意为想象或幻影。

items.en: Fantaisie meant imagination or a whim.

items.en: Fantasie and fantsy named imagination.

items.en: Fancy shortened the word and added the sense of taste.

definition_zh: 贷款；借款；出借；借用物；借词
definition_en: money lent on the understanding that it will be repaid, or any thing lent for temporary use
core_image: 一只手把一叠钱推过桌面，桌对面的人签下一张写有归还日期的纸
scene: 年底，小店老板在银行签下文件，拿到一笔钱用于进货，约定按月归还。 The shop took out a loan to buy stock for the winter.
sceneCN: 这里 loan 指「贷款」（第 1 个义项：借出并约定归还的钱）；句意为这家小店取得一笔贷款来备冬季存货。图中可辨识物件：合同、钞票、日历、签字笔；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 贷款；借款；借用物；借词（可数）

senses.title: Money lent for repayment
senses.definition: a sum of money given to a borrower on condition that it is paid back, usually with interest
senses.definitionCN: 交给借款人、约定归还（通常附利息）的一笔钱
senses.example: The shop took out a loan to buy stock for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小店取得一笔贷款来备冬季存货。
senses.why: the core of the word is a thing handed over temporarily, and money is the thing most often handed over on those terms.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是临时交出的东西，而钱是最常按这种条件交出的东西。

senses.title: The act of lending
senses.definition: the act or arrangement of lending something, as in the making of a loan
senses.definitionCN: 借出某物的行为或安排，如放贷
senses.example: The loan was arranged in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款在一个下午就办妥了。
senses.why: English uses the same noun for the act and the object, so a loan can name the transaction as well as the sum.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个名词指行为和物件，因此 loan 既可指交易，也可指金额。

senses.title: An object lent temporarily
senses.definition: a thing other than money lent for temporary use, such as a book or a tool
senses.definitionCN: 除金钱外临时借出的物品，如书或工具
senses.example: The library made a loan of the atlas for one week.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆把地图册外借一周。
senses.why: the money sense is the dominant one, but the older general sense of a thing lent never disappeared.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义占主导，但「借出之物」这一更早的泛指义从未消失。

senses.title: A word borrowed from another language
senses.definition: a word taken into one language from another, usually shortened from loanword
senses.definitionCN: 从另一种语言进入某种语言的词，通常是 loanword 的缩略
senses.example: Sushi is a loan in English from Japanese.
senses.exampleCN: sushi 是英语从日语借来的借词。
senses.why: linguists extended the money metaphor to words, which are borrowed and never returned.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把金钱比喻扩展到词上：词被借走，却从不归还。

senses.title: To lend, as a verb
senses.definition: to give something to someone for temporary use, especially in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 把某物交给他人临时使用，尤见于美式用法
senses.example: The bank loaned the money at a fixed rate.
senses.exampleCN: 银行以固定利率贷出这笔钱。
senses.why: the verb is a later back-formation from the noun and remains less common than lend in British English.
senses.whyCN: 动词义是从名词后起的逆构，在英式英语中仍不如 lend 常用。

senses.title: A temporarily transferred player
senses.definition: in sport, a player allowed to play for another club for a period while still under contract
senses.definitionCN: 体育中仍在原俱乐部合同期内、被允许为另一俱乐部短期出赛的球员
senses.example: The young striker joined on loan until June.
senses.exampleCN: 这名年轻前锋以租借形式加盟到六月。
senses.why: a player is the object lent: the owning club keeps the contract, the other club gets temporary use.
senses.whyCN: 球员就是被借出的对象：原俱乐部保留合同，另一俱乐部获得临时使用权。

senses.title: A work lent for an exhibition
senses.definition: a painting or object lent by one museum to another for a show
senses.definitionCN: 一家博物馆借给另一家用于展览的画作或器物
senses.example: The portrait is a loan from a private collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像是从私人收藏借展的作品。
senses.why: museums use the word because ownership stays put while the object travels temporarily.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆用这个词，因为物件临时出门而所有权留在原处。

senses.title: A temporary grant, figuratively
senses.definition: a short grant of something immaterial, such as time, attention or confidence
senses.definitionCN: 对无形之物的短期给予，如时间、关注或信心
senses.example: Time is a generous lender of second chances.
senses.exampleCN: 时间总是大方地借出重来的机会。
senses.why: the metaphor treats time and trust as things lent rather than given, since they must be returned in some form.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把时间与信任当作借出而非给出之物，因为它们终须以某种形式归还。

intro.en: Loan is a Scandinavian borrowing into English, not a Latin word. It is closely tied to lend, and the two descend from one Germanic idea. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: loan 是英语从斯堪的纳维亚语借入的词，并非拉丁词。它与 lend 关系密切，两者源自同一个日耳曼概念。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old Norse lán meant 'loan, something lent'; it entered English during the Viking settlements and settled into the everyday vocabulary.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 lán 意为「借款、被借出之物」，在维京人定居时期进入英语，并落入日常词汇。

items.en: Old English had læn 'loan' and lænan 'to lend'; the native noun was later replaced in most uses by the Scandinavian form.
items.cn: 古英语有 læn「借款」与 lænan「借出」；本族名词后来在多数用法中被斯堪的纳维亚形式取代。

items.en: The Germanic stock is generally traced to a root meaning 'to leave', so that a loan is literally something left with another person.
items.cn: 这套日耳曼词一般被追溯到表示「留下」的词根，因此借款字面上就是留在别人手里的东西。

items.en: That root would make loan a distant relative of Latin linquere 'to leave', but the connection is a reconstruction and not a borrowing from Latin.
items.cn: 若该词根成立，loan 便是拉丁 linquere「留下」的远亲；但这一联系属重构形式，并非从拉丁语借入。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as lone or lane; the modern spelling with -oa- is a later convention.
items.cn: 中世纪英语把这个词写作 lone 或 lane；现代带 -oa- 的拼法是后来的惯例。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact first record in English is not fixed, and the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：它在英语中的最早记录没有定论，日耳曼语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that share the lending stem; group two holds financial words that overlap with loan but differ in who owes and who owns.
note.cn: 第一组是共用「借出」词干的形式；第二组是与 loan 重叠、但在「谁欠谁、谁拥有」上不同的金融词。

entries.definition: The native verb for giving something temporarily; loan as a verb is its American twin.
entries.definitionCN: 本族动词，表示临时给出；作动词的 loan 是它的美式孪生形式。

entries.definition: One who lends; the ending -er marks the giver, not the thing given.
entries.definitionCN: 出借的人；词尾 -er 标记给予者，而非被给予之物。

entries.definition: The person who receives a loan; -ee marks the receiver, the mirror of -er.
entries.definitionCN: 接受贷款的人；-ee 标记接受者，与 -er 相对。

entries.definition: Meaning 'solitary', from a different stem; it sounds exactly like loan but shares no history.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「孤单的」，词干不同；读音与 loan 完全相同，却无共同来源。

entries.definition: The trust that allows goods or money to be given before payment; a loan is the sum so given.
entries.definitionCN: 允许先给货或钱后付款的信任；loan 是据此给出的款项。

entries.definition: A loan secured on property; it is one kind of loan, not a synonym for all loans.
entries.definitionCN: 以财产作担保的贷款；是贷款的一种，并非所有贷款的统称。

entries.definition: The obligation created by a loan; the loan is the money handed over, the debt is what remains owed.
entries.definitionCN: 贷款产生的偿付义务；loan 是交出的钱，debt 是仍欠的部分。

entries.definition: Money paid before it is due, often to a worker or supplier; it may or may not be repaid.
entries.definitionCN: 在到期前支付的款项，常给工人或供应商；可能需偿还，也可能不必。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Loan came from Old Norse, and lend is its native English cousin from the same Germanic idea.
normal.cn: loan 来自古诺斯语，lend 是同一日耳曼概念下的英语本族表亲。

normal.en: The family runs loan, lend, lender, loanee, loanable, loanword and reloan.
normal.cn: 同族包括 loan、lend、lender、loanee、loanable、loanword 与 reloan。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: take out a loan, pay off a loan, a student loan, on loan.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：取得贷款、还清贷款、学生贷款、借来的。

normal.en: Loan and lone sound alike but have no shared history.
normal.cn: loan 与 lone 读音相同，却没有共同来源。

normal.en: Museums and football clubs both say on loan when ownership stays put.
normal.cn: 博物馆与足球俱乐部都用 on loan，表示所有权留在原处。

abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币递过桌面，绳子的另一端仍系在给出者手上。

abstract.en: Picture a borrowed book that returns with someone else's notes in the margin.
abstract.cn: 想象一本借出的书回来时页边写着别人的批注。

examples.en: She took the novel on loan from the library.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「loan 借出」——钱借出去，约期归还 → 贷款、借用物

root: 古诺斯语 lán「借款、借出之物」，与古英语 læn、动词 lænan「借出」同源；这套词一般追溯到表示「留下」的日耳曼词根，与拉丁 linquere「留下」的更深联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: something is handed over for temporary use and must come back, whether money, a book, a player, a painting, a word or a little time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物交出供临时使用，并终须归还，无论那是钱、书、球员、画作、词，还是一点时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin pushed across a table with a string still tied to the giver.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币被推过桌面，绳子的另一端仍系在给出者手上。

branches.en: MONEY AND ITS ACT: the sum lent and the transaction share one noun.
branches.cn: 钱与行为：借出的金额与这笔交易共用一个名词。

branches.en: OBJECTS THAT TRAVEL: a book or a painting leaves its owner for a while and returns.
branches.cn: 出门的物件：书或画暂时离开主人，然后再回来。

branches.en: WORDS THAT NEVER RETURN: a borrowed word stays in the new language for good.
branches.cn: 不再归还的词：借词永久留在新语言里。

branches.en: THE VERB FORM: the same transaction seen as an action rather than a thing.
branches.cn: 动词形式：同一笔交易被看作动作而非物件。

branches.en: TEMPORARY GRANTS: a player and a stretch of time are both lent without being given away.
branches.cn: 暂时的给予：球员与一段时间都是借出，而非送出。

intro.en: Loan is a whole Scandinavian word, so its family is built by adding English endings to loan or to its native twin lend, not by peeling off Latin parts.
intro.cn: loan 是一个完整的斯堪的纳维亚词，因此它的词族靠给 loan 或其本族孪生词 lend 加英语词尾构成，而不是拆拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word stands behind loan; Latin expressed the idea with mutuum, which is not related in form. Any link through the root for 'leave' is a reconstruction at a deeper level.
latinIntro.cn: loan 背后没有拉丁词；拉丁语用 mutuum 表达这一概念，而它在形式上并无关联。通过「留下」词根建立的联系属更深层的重构形式。

senses.title: Land of a state
